fatal_errors: The proposed Cu segregation/CuO lubrication mechanism is unsupported by any cited evidence and is not the mechanism indicated by the target.

The predicted reduction in friction and wear at high temperature contradicts the target result: above about 900 K, lattice disorder increases, hardness and wear resistance fall, and friction rises and fluctuates strongly.
The intervention replaces temperature-dependent nanoindentation/friction testing of a defined FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system with an unspecified annealing treatment and oxidative tribology experiment.
The loading boundary is not quantitatively defined, so the claimed service regime is not reproducible.
explanation: The hypothesis remains broadly aligned with thin-film, high-temperature wear and provides a comparative experiment with measurable microstructure, chemistry, friction, and wear outcomes. However, it does not reconstruct the central temperature-driven mechanism. The target attributes the transition near 900 K to rapid lattice disorder, reduced dislocation density, changing HCP/stacking-fault populations, and consequent softening; the generated hypothesis instead introduces annealing-induced Cu segregation and oxidation in an atmosphere not present in the target conditions. It also predicts beneficial high-temperature lubrication, opposite to the observed sharp decline in wear resistance and increase in friction. Although the proposed experiment could test its own mechanism, absent supporting evidence it is a speculative alternative rather than a well-supported one.
